docs.creator: Baraka, Amiri
docs.description: Amiri Baraka prepares a class for a musical performance. He creates a bass line, assigns students to categories of musical instruments, and tells them they will be playing against his recording of the bass line. He goes over basic rhythmic concepts. The tape ends abruptly.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Amiri Baraka class, The poet orchestra, August, 1985.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Allen Ginsberg presents a class on "Spiritual Poetics." Ginsberg discusses the influence of haiku on the Beats and the relative merits of tape recorders and notebooks for writing poetry. He then reads and comments on selections from the Collected Earlier Poems of William Carlos Williams. (Continued on 74P003). This is part 2 of 3.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class Spiritual Poetics part 2

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Tape 6 of an 11 tape series of a class taught by Allen Ginsberg on Expansive Poetics. Ginsberg discusses the lives and writing of Anna Akhmatova and Sergey Yesenin.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Class 6 Expansive Poetics

docs.creator: Augustine, Jane
docs.description: Tape 1 of 2 containing a class taught by Jane Augustine. Topics include gender politics, the power structures inherent in sex, and Buddhism. Augustine cites the work of such writers as Helen Cixous, Luce Iragaray, and Julia Kristeva.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Jane Augustine class on gender identity part 1 July 1991

docs.creator: Snyder, Gary
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Gary Snyder Class Part 2 1983

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: First half of a class with Allen Ginsberg reading and discussing the work of Walt Whitman and William Wordsworth, focusing on their later work. Ginsberg reads examples of Whitman's prose and poems, including "Sands at Seventy," Wordsworth's "Tintern Abbey," and examples of Wordsworth's "bad poetry." Ginsberg also reads and discusses Wordsworth's sonnets in favor of capital punishment, "Sonnets on the Punishment of Death." (Continues on 76p072.)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
subject: New American Poetry
beat movement
political poetry
transcendental poetry
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class on Walt Whitman and William Wordsworth - Part 1

docs.creator: Burroughs, William S.
docs.description: William S. Burroughs reads from "The Place of Dead Roads" and "The Cat Inside." Keywords: beat movement, experimental writing
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: William S. Burroughs reading.

docs.creator: Bernstein, Charles
docs.description: A lecture by Charles Bernstein on poetics. Bernstein reads from "Fragments from the 17th Manifesto of Nude Formalism by Hermes Hermeneutic" and "The Second War." Discussion includes the holocaust, Heidegger, racism, radical modernism, the effects of World War II on American culture, and Reznikoff's "Holocaust." The lecture ends with a question and answer session.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
subject: New American Poetry
political poetry
war in literature
antiwar literature
docs.title: Charles Bernstein lecture on poetics

docs.creator: Smith, Harry
docs.description: A class with Harry Smith showing a movie and commenting on it.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
subject: mysticism
consciousness
docs.title: Harry Smith class.

docs.creator: Whalen, Philip
docs.description: Second half of Class 7 of "In the Pressure Tank" series held at Naropa Institute between July 23 and August 20, 1980. (The whole series is contained on 80P093-115.) Philip Whalen discusses Hart Crane's poem "For the Marriage of Faustus and Helen." (Continued from 80p103.)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
subject: New American Poetry
West Coast poetry
Buddhism
symbolism
American Modernist poetry
docs.title: In the pressure tank, Class 7 - Part 2

docs.creator: Whalen, Philip
docs.description: First half of Class 10 of "In the Pressure Tank" series held at Naropa Institute between July 23 and August 20, 1980. (The whole series is contained on 80P093-115.) Philip Whalen discusses Hart Crane's poem "The Bridge", continuing the discussion from the previous meeting of the class and focusing on the literary and historical context of the poem. He also looks at the work of Lew Welch. (Continues on 80p110.)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
subject: New American Poetry
West Coast poetry
Buddhism
symbolism
American Modernist poetry
docs.title: In the pressure tank, Class 10 - Part 1

docs.creator: Whalen, Philip
docs.description: First half of Class 7 of "In the Pressure Tank" series held at Naropa Institute between July 23 and August 20, 1980. (The whole series is contained on 80P093-115.) Philip Whalen discusses Hart Crane's poem "For the Marriage of Faustus and Helen." (Continues on 80p104.)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
subject: New American Poetry
West Coast poetry
Buddhism
symbolism
American Modernist poetry
docs.title: In the pressure tank, Class 7 - Part 1

docs.creator: Elmslie, Kenward; Taylor, Steven
docs.description: Kenward Elmslie and Steven Taylor perform "various gobbets" from Postcards on parade, Elmslie's musical play written in response to the AIDS epidemic. Elmslie explains that the show is written to be performed by a cast of eight and invites the members of the audience to fill in the missing pieces in their minds.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Kenward Elmslie and Steven Taylor performance, Postcards on parade, July, 1994.

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: Second half of a class from Anne Waldman's month-long series on female writers, "Some Women Writers," during the summer of 1977. This class is about Emily Dickinson. Her life and work are discusssed in great detail. Anne reads Dickinson's work and offers information on Dickinson's biography, poetry, and letters. (Continued from 77p068.) Keyword: New American Poetry, New York School, women poets, feminist poetry, spiritualism and literature
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman class on poetics and female writers.

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: First half of a class from Anne Waldman's month-long series on female writers, "Some Women Writers," during the summer of 1977, focusing on the life and work of Gertrude Stein. The class includes student discussion with Waldman lecturing on Stein's life and style of writing, readings from Stein's books Lifting Belly, Three Lives, and Tender Buttons, and a brief introduction to the plays of Christopher Knowles. (Continued on 77P082.)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman class on poetics and female writers, August, 1977.

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: A class in a series by Anne Waldman, "Poet as Shaman," part 4. Waldman discusses Louis Zukovsky's translations of Dante and defines candidates for shamanism. (Series continues on 79P038)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman class, Poet as shaman, part 8, July, 1979.

docs.creator: Mayer, Bernadette
docs.description: Bernadette Mayer gives a lecture in which she talks about her intentions relating to the books she has published to this date. Her overall purpose is to explain the structure and processes she used for putting together her creative books. She reads selections from Utopia and Sonnets, and mentions her two non-fiction prose works, Handbook of poetic forms and Art of sciene writing. The creative books she discusses are: Story, Ceremony Latin 1964, Moving, Memory, Studying hunger, Poetry, Euruditio ex memoria, The golden book of words, Midwinter day, Utopia, and Sonnets.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Bernadette Mayer Lecture

docs.creator: Vicuna, Cecilia
docs.description: Chilean poet Cecilia Vicuna performance at the Boulder Museum of Contemporary Art. Vicuna uses words in Spanish and English, a capella singing, non-verbal vocal sounds, and other sound effects in her performance concerning the significance of September 11th in Chilean history, among other topics.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Cecelia Vicuna performance, July, 2002.

docs.creator: diPrima, Diane; Ginsberg, Allen; Waldman, Anne
docs.description: First half of a reading by Allen Ginsberg, Anne Waldman, and Diane diPrima. Some of the readings included are Waldman's "Fast Speaking Woman," Ginsberg's "A Manifesto," and diPrima's "Loba." (Continues on 74p009.) Keywords: New American Poetry, beat movement, feminist poetry, incantation, protest poetry, political poetry
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: A reading by Allen Ginsberg, Anne Waldman, and Diane diPrima.

docs.creator: Taylor, Steven
docs.description: First half of a Steven Taylor lecture on performance. He plays and discusses recordings of performances by a variety of artists including Tuli Kupferberg, Kenward Elmslie, Ed Sanders, and the Fugs, and offers tips on collaboration, the voice, and performance. (Continued on 87P052)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Steven Taylor performs class on performance, with Tuli Kupferburg of the Fugs, July, 1987.

docs.creator: Coolidge, Clark
docs.description: A Clark Coolidge lecture on Samuel Beckett, with particular focus on Beckett's prose. Much of the lecture is Coolidge performing a cut-up reading of Beckett's lesser-known, many unpublished, prose works.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Clark Coolidge lecture, July, 1989.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: This is the 17th session of a class in basic poetics taught by Allen Ginsberg in 1980 at the Naropa Institute. In this class, Ginsberg reads and discusses a number of songs by Shakespeare. During the last part of the class the students recite spontaneous poems. This is class 17 of 33.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Basic Poetics, Class 17

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: A literature class, "Basic Poetics," taught by Allen Ginsberg at The Naropa Institiute May 15, 1980. For the duration of the class Ginsberg discusses Saphhic meter using various poems to demonstrate the ancient form. This is class 29 of 33.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Basic Poetics class 29

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: The first session of a class in basic poetics taught by Allen Ginsberg in 1980 at Naropa Institute. This session discusses Shakespeare's poetry and the Lyric and Ballad poets, juxtaposing these with Modernist, Futurist, and contemporary poets such as William Carlos Williams, Ezra Pound, Charles Reznikoff, and David Cope, to show the evolution and direction of poetics. Ginsberg ends the session by reading extensively from Cope's selected works. This is class 1 of 33.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Basic Poetics class 1 January 1980

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Allen Ginsberg class on Expansive Poetry. This class begins with AG talking about the change in writing as time and technology progressed with repsect to voyage writing and travel accounts. He reads from Carpenter's "The secret of time and satan" and then there is a digressive conversation about meditation and being mindful and the San Franscisco New School. Then the class reads Dunan's "The lightfoot hears you and the darkness begins" and there is talk about the Whitmanesque quality of the writing they are reading in this class. The class closes with more commentary about Carpenter and AG reading his "From Tourin to Paris."
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Class July 1981

docs.creator: Charters, Ann; Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Allen Ginsberg and Ann Charters class discussing and reading from Russian Futurists. Topics include Sergei Esenin's book Confessions of a Hooligan, Vladimir Mayakovsky's poem "A Cloud in trousers," Mayakovsky's biography and prison story, rebellion's relationship to Punk, utopian heroic Communism, linguistic exploration, and Lenin and Trotsky on Russia's $150 million loan.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg and Ann Charters class on Russian Futurists, July, 1981.

docs.creator: Corso, Gregory; Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: A class on the history of poetry by Allen Ginsberg, in a series of classes from 1975. Ginsburg discusses William Shakespeare and Ben Johnson in detail. Putting poetry to music, and the poet James Shirley are also discussed.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class,the history of poetry, part 10, June, 1975.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: This is a class on Shakespeare's Tempest, taught by Allen Ginsberg, from August 18, 1980 at Naropa. At the outset, Ginsberg explains that instead of reading the whole play through, he will touch on important lines in each Act and scene and explore them deeply. In this recording he discusses Act I scene 1 and 2 with various digressions and explications on Shakespeare's metaphores, Aristotle's poetic and dramatic theories, Ezra Pound's four parts of poetry, and Ginsberg's own poetic influences from Shakespreare with asides about Jack Kerouac, William S. Burroughs, Bob Dylan, and Gregory Corso. This is class 1 of 4.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class 1

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: A continuation of a class on Shakespeare's Tempest, Allen Ginsberg draws parallels between Gregory Corso and Shakespeare, reading verse by both authors. Later Allen goes deeper into the text of Act I of Shakespeare's Tempest. This is class 2 of 4.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class 2 August 1980

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: Anne Waldman, Rotating Shakespeare: Troilus and Cressida, June 1980. Waldman presents a second class on Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida, discussing the post-apocalyptic quality of the play, Shakespeare's genius, the nihilism and "modernity" of the play, its status as a "problem play" and its relationships with other of Shakespeare's problem plays. A love scene from Romeo and Juliet is compared with a love scene from Troilus and Cressida, and a passage from Milton is read to show connections between the "Latinate diction" of the play and that of future works. (Continued on 80P142). This is class 3 of 4.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman class 3 June 1980

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: A class in a series by Anne Waldman, "Poet as Shaman," part 10. Class topics include Michael McClure's "Ghost Tantras," Buddhism in the Kerouac School, and Hugo Ball.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman class, Poet as shaman, part 10, July, 1979.

docs.creator: Taylor, Steven
docs.description: First half of a Steven Taylor lecture on the history of music, beginning with music in ancient Egypt, Sumer, and Greece and moving on to the evolution of music in European countries. He discusses the Greek modes and plays examples of music from different periods. The lecture ends with a recording of an Ed Sanders musical setting of a latin phrase. (Continued on 86P053)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Steven Taylor class on ancient Greek music, July, 1986.

docs.creator: Alexander, Charles; Ortiz, Simon; Waldman, Anne; Wilson, Peter Lamborn
docs.description: This tape contains the end of the final poem read by Simon Ortiz on Tape 01P071. This is part 2 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Faculty reading part 2 Ortiz July 2001

docs.creator: Baraka, Prevallet, & Richards
docs.description: This faculty reading includes Amiri Baraka reading "Somebody Blew Up America" and "The Mind of the President" and talking about his murdered daughter; Kristin Prevallet reading predominantly political pieces such as "Force," "Norm" and "Blueprint for a Revolution"; and Deborah Richards reading "Notes from the Margin," "Some Notes from a Looseleaf War Journal," and "Author's Note." This is part 1 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Faculty reading with Baraka, Prevallet, Richards part 1

docs.creator: Cope, David; Micheline, Jack; Orlovsky, Peter
docs.description: This is one of the evening readings of the Kerouac Conference. David Cope reads a selection of poems, they are from a recent book that is published as well as old and new work. Then Jack Micheline reads. I very powerful performance that combines sounds of jazz and his unique way of living. The Orlovsky reads one poem as a favor to the audience. The evening ends.[by Ann] An open reading with David Cope, Jack Micheline, and Peter Orlovsky in a mall in Boulder, Colorado. Cope's selections include The rose, The workman, and At the resthome, among others. Micheline explains that his poetry incorporates the sounds of jazz. He reads Conversation with Jack Kerouac and other poems, sings songs, reads a statement on poetry, and talks about how Jack Kerouac wrote the introduction to his book, River of red wine. Orlovsky reads Signature changed.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Kerouac Conference holmes workshop part 4 1982

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: Second half of an Anne Waldman workshop on writing. The class begins with a discussion about what led people to come to the conference. Waldman talks about how she became involved with the Beats and came to Boulder, the founding of Naropa, and Kerouac's influence on the school. She reads and discusses part of an interview with William Carlos Williams, about writing poetry, and selections from Gertrude Stein, Vladimir Mayakovsky, and other poets. Students read their work and Waldman comments and makes suggestions. (Continued from 82P317A)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman workshop, Kerouac conference, June, 1982.

docs.creator: Mayer, Bernadette
docs.description: Second half of a Bernadette Mayer class on experimental techniques in writing and other arts. She reads some of the writing of Tristan Tzara, Antonin Artaud, Eric Satie, Gertrude Stein, and others, and discusses Dada, the unconscious, cut-ups, and sentence structure. (Continued on 78P081)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Bernadette Mayer class on experimental writing techniques, June, 1978.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Second half of an Allen Ginsberg lecture on English and American lyric poetry. Ginsberg reads Sir Walter Raleigh's "The lie," Christophr Marlowe's "The passionate shepherd to his love," Hector Berlioz and Giuseppe Verdi requiems, George Peel's "As when the rye reached to the chin" and "Hot sun, cool fire, tempered with sweet air, and Robert Southwell's "The burning babe." (Continued from 96P049)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg lecture on English and American lyric poetry, July, 1996.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: A literature class, "Basic Poetics," taught by Allen Ginsberg at The Naropa Institute March 27, 1980. Ginsberg begins discussing the prosody of Robert Creeley then segues into the bulk of the lecture centered around the poetry of the English Metaphysical poet John Donne. This is class 19 of 33.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Basic Poetics, Class 19

docs.creator: Charters, Ann; Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Author and editor Ann Charters joins Allen Ginsberg for a class focusing on the work and life of Russian poet Vladimir Mayakovsky. Ginsberg and Charters discuss Mayakovsky's poetry, including "Lenin," "About this," "On the nature of love," "Sergei Yesinin," and "At the top of my voice," his play "The bedbug," his love affairs and his work for, and complicated relationship with, the Communist Party.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg and Anne Charters lecture on Vladimir Mayakovsky, July, 1981.

docs.creator: Eshleman, Clayton
docs.description: A lecture with Clayton Eshleman including readings from Aime Cesaire's Notebook of a Return to the Native Land with topics including Martinique life, thematic narrative, surrealism, translation, neologisms, movements within it. He also reads from Les Armes Miraculeuses and Corpus Perdu, then discusses how Cesaire's poetry influences his own work. Keywords: New American Poetry, translation, negritude
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Clayton Eshleman lecture: "At the locks of the void, translating the work of Aime Cesaire."

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: One in a series of classes given by Anne Waldman on the work of Gertrude Stein at the Naropa Institute. In this class Waldman focuses on Stein's play Four saints in three acts, reading from the play and discussing its background, language, and production.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman Class August 1978

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Second half of an Allen Ginsberg class on his mentor William Carlos Williams. Ginsberg compares the work and influences of Wordsworth, Whitman, and Reznikov, and reads from Williams's "Prelude," "Cambridge in the Alps," "Rain," and others. He gives examples of Williams's writing techniques and relates some of them to the meditative mind. (Continued from 87P013)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Ginsberg class on Williams part 2 July 1987

docs.creator: Ducornet, Rikki; Ellsworth, Michelle; Field, Thalia; Fleisher, Kass; Pate, Alexs
docs.description: Rikki Ducornet chairs a panel on Voice and Chararcter delivered July 1st, 2003, at Naropa University. Panelists include, Kass Fleisher on the political structures of the sentence and creating a paralell structures in prose to overcome the traditional structures of prose; Michelle Ellsworth discusses the voice as character in performance; Alexs Pate discusses how in his work he seeks to appropriate the traditional structers of prose to create a new space; and Thalia Field discusses the uses of voice searching for a character in prose. The Panel is followed by a Q&A session which heats up when the panelists decide to turn it into an all out argument (particularly between Alexs and Kass) circling questions from the audience.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Panel called Voice and Character July 1, 2003

docs.creator: DuCharme, Mark; Ginsberg, Allen; Hawkins, Bobbie Louise; Hollo, Anselm; Waldman, Anne
docs.description: Reading of Ted Berrigan's Sonnets. Naropa students, faculty, and friends read Berrigan's Sonnets in "round-robin" style.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Reading of Berrigan Sonnets July 1993

docs.creator: Gilbert, Alan; Hunt, Laird
docs.description: A reading, tape 2 of 2, given by Alan Gilbert and Laird Hunt at Naropa University June 19, 2004. Gilbert reads from two long poems in progress. Hunt reads from a selection of prose concluding with 1 1/2 chapters from his manuscript Dear Laird Hunt Author of The Impossibly." This is part 2 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Reading with Gilbert, Hunt part 2 June 2004

docs.creator: Clay, Steve; Wille, Andrew
docs.description: A Steve Clay interview, Conversation on Craft. Andrew Wille interviews Steve Clay about being the publisher of Granary Books. They focus on the history, the process, the technology, and the use of collaboration.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Steve Clay Interview Conversation on Craft June 2004

docs.creator: Rothenberg, Jerome
docs.description: Jerome Rothenberg class on ethnopoetics and performance, discussing sacred performance and clowns, including Barbara Tedlock's book Teachings from the American Earth, Elsie Parson's book Pueblo Indian Religion, Black Elk's description of sacred clowns, Crow Indian sacred clowns, the relationship between clown and shaman, sexual behavior among Pueblo clowns, proto clowns, trickster gods and Balinese clowns. Part 5 of a series.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Jerome Rothenberg class on ethnopoetics and performance, August, 1981, part 5.

docs.creator: Hawkins, Bobbie Louise; Rothenberg, Jerome
docs.description: Jerome Rothenberg class on ethnopoetics and performance discussing Seneca ceremonies, difficulties with serious poetry on TV, technology and individual experience, the dangers of obsessiveness, using comedy as a remedy, and the function of music. There is also an off-topic student discussion early in the class.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Jerome Rothenberg class on ethnopoetics and performance, August, 1981.

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne
docs.description: This is class II of a series taught by Joanne Kyger at the Naropa Institute in 1981 entitled Compassion for Place. Kyger continues to discuss Coyote in brief, but focuses the main part of the class on the poetry of Native American poet Simon Ortiz, which she reads extensively for about 40 minutes with light discussion of the work intermittently. This is class 2 of 12.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Joanne Kyger class 2 June 1981

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Second half of an Allen Ginsberg workshop for On the road: The Jack Kerouac conference, sponsored by the Naropa Institute. Ginsberg discusses rhythm, poetry and rhyme. The workshop ends with a question and answer session. (Continued from 82P316B)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: On the road: The Jack Kerouac conference, Allen Ginsberg workshop, July, 1982.

docs.creator: Whalen, Philip
docs.description: First half of Class 7 of "In the Pressure Tank" series held at Naropa Institute between July 23 and August 20, 1980. (The whole series is contained on 80P093-115.) Philip Whalen discusses Hart Crane's poem "For the Marriage of Faustus and Helen." (Continues on 80p104.) Keywords: New American Poetry, West Coast poetry, Buddhism, American modernist poetry, symbolism
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: In the pressure tank, Class 7

docs.creator: Whalen, Philip
docs.description: First half of a Philip Whalen class on Igor Stravinsky. After spending the first part of the class talking about rowdy poetry readings, Whalen discusses Stravinsky's ideas about time, order, and the creative process, then looks at how they apply to writing poetry. Whalen also tells anecdotes from Stravinsky's life, and talks about the sources for his music. (Continues on 77P030)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Philip Whalen class, part 4, August 1977.

docs.creator: Chogyam Trungpa, Rinpoche; Rome, David
docs.description: A reading of Chogyam Trungpa Rinpoche's poetry written in English, as well as his poetry written in Tibetan and translated into English by Trungpa Rinpoche with British and American friends. Trungpa Rinpoche introduces each poem and reads portions in the original Tibetan accompanied by David Rome reading the English texts.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Chogyam Trungpa Rinpoche Tibetan poetry reading with English translations by David Rome, August, 1975.

docs.creator: Torres, Edwin
docs.description: First half of an Edwin Torres lecture that is as much poetic performance as intellectual talk. He weaves together three pieces, "The limit is limitless," "The impossible sentence," and "The popadology of an ambient language," to create an almost seamless meditation on the evolution of poetry through performance, interference as freedom, what we miss in language, other possibilities of perception, and the timelessness and importance of ambient sound. (Continues on 03P086)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Edwin Torres lecture, The limit is limitless, July, 2003.

docs.creator: Rakosi, Carl
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Cope and Rakosi read part 2 June 1987

docs.creator: Spahr, Juliana
docs.description: Juliana Spahr presents a short lecture on Bernadette Mayer's sonnets. Spahr questions the use of traditional forms by women writers as a gesture of resistance and/or subversion. In the question and answer session, Spahr and the audience discuss possible uses of lyricism that might problematize conventional discourses of sexuality and gender.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Juliana Spahr lecture on Bernadette Mayer, June, 2000.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: A literature class, "Basic Poetics," taught by Allen Ginsberg at The Naropa Institure April 10, 1980. Ginsberg and class discuss and read from the works of Ben Jonson and Robert Herrick. Ginsberg focuses mostly on the prosody of these to poet's work. This is class 22 of 33.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Basic Poetics, Class 22

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen; Taylor, Steven; Waldman, Anne
docs.description: First half of a poetry reading at Naropa Institute with Allen Ginsberg, Anne Waldman, Amiri Baraka, and Steven Taylor performing songs. Ginsberg reads "Howl" and "Footnote to Howl." Taylor sings "The virus will take one in ten" and "As I walked out one morning." Waldman reads "May I speak thus" and other poems. Baraka reads "The mind of the president," "The best kept secret," "Masked angel costume," "Changes Changing," "X," "Funk lore," "I am" and other poems. (Continues on 92P032)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg, Anne Waldman, and Amiri Baraka reading with Steven Taylor song performance, July, 1992.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Literary History of the Beat Generation, Class #13, taught by Allen Ginsberg. Topics covered: Kerouac's sketching in "Book of Dreams" and "Visions of Cody."
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class, Literary history of the Beat generation, the 50's, part 13, May, 1981.

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: Second half of the final class from Anne Waldman's month-long series on female writers, "Some Women Writers," during the summer of 1977, primarily consisting of student presentations. Each student reports on a subject that they have chosen for further study and then presents that subject to the entire class. Waldman makes a few closing remarks and reads from Gertrude Stein's "Why do you feel differently?" (Continued from 77P083)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman class on poetics and female writers, August, 1977.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Tape 5 of an 11 tape series of a class taught by Allen Ginsberg on Expansive Poetics. Subject matter includes background on such movements as the Futurists, Acmeists, and Imaginists as well as readings of work by various artists including Osip Mandelstam, Jorge Ivanov, Nikolai Gumilev, William Carlos Williams, and Anna Akhmatova.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Class 5 Expansive Poetics

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: First half of part 4 of an Allen Ginsberg workshop on American value. Ginsberg discusses the work of William Carlos Williams, including the poems "The trees," "To a friend," and "Poor old Abner." (Continues on 87P086)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class, American value, part 4, March, 1987.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: A literature class taught by Allen Ginsberg at The Naropa Institute, April 14, 1980. Ginsberg and class read and discuss the poetry of Hart Crane, George Herbert, Henry King and Dylan Thomas. Ginsberg also speaks extensively about the notions of condensation, vision and meter. This is class 23 of 33.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Basic Poetics, Class 23

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Tape 11 of an 11 tape series of Allen Ginsberg's class on Expansive Poetics. Subject matter includes background on such Russian writers as Kaysin Kuliev and Sergei Yesenin. Also included are readings of work by Gordon McVay, Vladimir Klebnikov, and Sergei Yesenin.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Class 11 Expansive Poetics

docs.creator: Hawkins, Bobbie Louise; Waldman, Anne
docs.description: First half of a class with Anne Waldman and Bobbie Louise Hawkins speaking on New American Poetry, including the theory and techniques of writing poetry, focusing on taking on other identities and voices as a writer. They read and discuss passages from a variety of writers including Gary Snyder, Robert Graves and Jerome Rothenberg. They discuss experimental writing techniques such as using the roots of words in order to generate new ideas and the role of the artist in society. Hawkins leads a performance exercise. (Continued on 88P064)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman and Bobbie Louise Hawkins class, I is another, July, 1988.

docs.creator: Thomas, Lorenzo
docs.description: Second half of a Lorenzo Thomas class on the history, context, and structure of blues songs. He plays and sings examples of blues songs including those of Robert Johnson, Bessie Smith, and Lightnin' Hopkins, and discusses them with the class. (Continued from 89P115)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Lorenzo Thomas class on blues songs, July, 1989.

docs.creator: Adam, Helen
docs.description: Second half of a lecture by Helen Adam, with this half focusing on English ballads, including "A Letter of Advice" and "Reputing Drive." (Continued from 79p025.) Keywords: New American Poetry, performance poetry, music in literature
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Helen Adam lecture.

docs.creator: Mayer, Bernadette
docs.description: Second portion of a Bernadette Mayer workshop on language poetry. The class reads some pieces by Charles Bernstein, Clark Coolidge's "Notes on Larry Eigner," Jackson McLow and selections out of the magazine Big Allis, including a piece by Dorothy Trujillo Lusk. The class then begins to read their personal language poetry pieces and discusses the new forms they have created and the background or rational for those forms. The class is continued on 89P092 and is part of a series with 89P075.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Bernadette Mayer workshop part 1

docs.creator: Cope, David; Corso, Gregory; Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: David Cope class. Cope talks about imagist and objectivist poetry. He reads several of his poems including "Baseball" and "The Stars." He and Allen Ginsberg dialogue about some other poets: Reznikov, Hartley, etc. Gregory Corso tells a story about Trungpa Rinpoche.continues on 80P125. This is class 4 of 4.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: David Cope part 4 July 1980

docs.creator: David Rome
docs.description: This is a tape of a David Rome lecture on topic: The Fruition of Peacemaking. Rome mostly explores Chogyam Trungpa Rinpoche's notion of enlightened society. He also discusses the mandala principle, the tension between the political and the spiritual, activism individually and in community, and "now-ness."
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: David Rome The Tradition of Peacemaking

docs.creator: Corso, Gregory
docs.description: Class instructed by Gregory Corso. The class covers various topics including the Beatnik image, Jack Kerouac, Big Sur, On the Road, and the old days at Naropa. This is class 6 of 8.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Gregory Corso class 6 August 1981

docs.creator: Aebi, Irene; Lacy, Steve
docs.description: Second half of a class by Steve Lacy and Irene Aebi discussing how they choose poems to set to music and the process of setting the piece to music. Lacy and Aebi perform "I cut the curtains of deception." They teach the class the song, "I said to joy." The class learns and sings the song while Lacy plays the piano. Other songs include "I know the truth," "Song of the woods," "I live like a cuckoo," "The whisper," "The smiles," "Sketches," and "Prison song." (Continued from 01P093)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Irene Aebi and Steve Lacy class, I sing the poets, July, 2001.

docs.creator: Randall, Margaret; Zamora, Daisy
docs.description: This is the final segment of a Margaret Randall workshop. In this continuation from 90P063, 90P064, 90P065, and 90P066 Daisy Zamora is discussing the recent election in Nicaragua that elected Violeta Chamorro. She discusses the campaigning, the 17.5 million dollars given to the Chamorro campaign by the US and the promises, vote buying, economic embargo and deflated spirit of the Nicaraguan people that all played apart in the election process. She details the different party promises and thoguhts of her people. There is much implication towards the US holding a major stake in which way the situation will play out based upon who they choose to support.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Margaret Randall Workshop part 3 July 1990

docs.creator: Charters, Ann
docs.description: First workshop of the Jack Kerouac conference, sponsored by the Naropa Institute in Boulder, Colorado. Anne Charters (biographer and Kerouac Scholar) tells how Kerouac's books have influenced her and a generation. She goes into detail about his style and the influence he had on her as well as her works. Her main focus is on Kerouac's book On The Road and how the book should be seen as one of the most important American novels.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: On the road: The Jack Kerouac conference, Ann Charters workshop, July, 1982.

docs.creator: Joris, Pierre
docs.description: A Pierre Joris lecture discussing the history of Arab poetry, including its development and relation to Arabic culture. He reads and discusses translated poems by several prominent writers, including Mahmoud Darwish, Abdul Kader El Janabi, and Abdellatif Laabi.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Pierre Joris lecture, Arabic poetics and the international literary scene, September, 2001.

docs.creator: Wilson, Peter Lamborn
docs.description: First half of a Peter Lamborn Wilson (aka Hakim Bey) lecture on the temporary autonomous zone, or the pleasures of disappearance. Wilson looks at the ways in which individuals and groups have created alternatives or found refuges from dominant repressive social realities. He gives examples of groups who created islands of autonomy in repressive cultures, such as pirates and colonists who joined the colonized. He also looks at how artists and writers have achieved temporary autonomous zones in terms of creativity, linguistics, and thought processes. Wilson concludes by proposing strategies for consciously creating temporary autonomous zones as a strategy for liberation. (Continued on 90P130. Note: The text of Wilson's lecture can be found online at http://www.hermetic.com/bey/taz3.html#labelPirateUtopias)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Peter Lamborn Wilson lecture, The temporary autonomous zone or the pleasures of disappearance, July, 1990.

docs.creator: Smith, Harry
docs.description: Harry Smith lecture on mythology and cultural practices in traditional and indigenous cultures. Among other topics, he discusses belief in reincarnation, the ceremonial use of peyote, and creation stories.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Harry Smith lecture on the Native American cosmos, July, 1990.

docs.creator: Mayer, Bernadette
docs.description: First half of a Bernadette Mayer class on experimental techniques in writing and other arts. She reads some of the writing of Tristan Tzara, Antonin Artaud, Eric Satie, Gertrude Stein, and others, and discusses Dada, the unconscious, cut-ups, and sentence structure. (Continues on 78P082)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Bernadette Mayer class on experimental writing techniques, June, 1978.

docs.creator: Tysh, Chris
docs.description: Chris Tysh workshop. Tysh presents an overview of possibilities for application (or possibly mis-application) of the theories of Marx, Freud, and Lacan to writing. Tysh concentrates on how writing can mirror-- in distorting and creative ways-- the world, the I, and experience.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Chris Tysh workshop 1991

docs.creator: Ferlinghetti, Lawrence; Ginsberg, Allen; Zamora, Daisy
docs.description: Daisy Zamora and Lawrence Ferlinghetti read original poetry, Allen Ginsberg reads poems by Nicanor Parra. Zamora's poems also read in English included, "Death's Makeup," and "What Hands in my Hands."
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Zamora Ferlinghetti poetry reading July 1990

docs.creator: Blaser, Robin
docs.description: A Robin Blaser lecture titled, Where's hell? Blaser reads and discusses portions of his Great companion piece on Dante Alighiere, a poetic commentary on Dante's ideas and use of language. Blaser discusses the works and ideas of other writiers including James Joyce, Percy Bysshe Shelley, Jean-Jacques Rousseau, Ludwig Wittgenstein and Ezra Pound.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.subject: none
docs.title: Robin Blaser lecture, Where's hell?, June, 1999.

docs.creator: Creeley, Robert
docs.description: Second half of a Robert Creeley lecture on the origins, history, politics, and techniques of language poetry. He looks at how language poetry evolved out of earlier styles as well as its influence on contemporary poets. Topics include the ideas of Charles Bernstein, the work of Charles Olson, William Carlos Williams, Robert Duncan, Ezra Pound, and many others, as well as the possibilities for using words without referents. (Continued from 84P009)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Robert Creeley lecture on language poetry, July, 1984.

docs.creator: Brown, Rebecca; Delany, Samuel R.; Evenson, Brian; Kapil Rider, Bhanu
docs.description: A Panel recorded June 22, 2004 during the Summer Writing Program at Naropa University, on Narrative and Identity, Brian Evenson, Chair. Panelists are Samuel R. "Chip" Delaney, Rebecca Brown, and Bhanu Kapil. Topics cover personal identity vs. narrative identity, writing from the other, experimental narrative and experimental identity, structure and identity, code and catagory in identity, stable and unstable identities and narrative. The Panel is followed with a Q&A.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Panel discussing personal identity vs. narrative identity June 2004

docs.creator: Wilson, Peter Lamborn
docs.description: Second half of a lecture by Peter Lamborn Wilson. This portion of the lecture is a question and answer session discussing topics such as cannabis culture, Native Americans and peyote use, and the Palestinian Liberation Front. (Continued from 99P053)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Peter Lamborn Wilson lecture, June, 1999.

docs.creator: Wilson, Peter Lamborn
docs.description: A Peter Lamborn Wilson lecture on the role of the poet in interpreting archaeology, anthropology, and human pre-history. He encourages poets to get involved in learning about these fields and taking on the task of interpreting the evidence, since scientists are reluctant to draw conclusions about the past. Wilson believes that we should move beyond interdisciplinary studies to what he calls "anti-categorization." During the course of the lecture he outlines some of his own ideas about the origin of consciousness, Neanderthal people, paleolithic writing, the Babylonian story of Marduk and Gilgamesh, and other aspects of early human history.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Peter Lamborn Wilson lecture, Plowing the clouds, July, 1994.

docs.creator: Baraka, Amiri; Ginsberg, Allen; Orlovsky, Peter; Ortiz, Simon
docs.description: Simon Ortiz reads from Fight Back and from Sand Creek. Peter Orlifsky plays a song on banjo, then monologues seeming improved. Diane Di Prima is wished a happy 50th birthday. Allen Ginsberg sings a few songs which are sound like earlier versions than found on Holy Soul Jelly Roll box set, and reads White Shroud. Amiri Baraka delivers a good performance with poems centered around African American history (wise) and Jazz.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Performance July 1984

docs.creator: Whalen, Philip
docs.description: First half of class 1 of "In the Pressure Tank" series held at Naropa Institute between July 23 and August 20, 1980. (The whole series is contained on 80P093-115.) Philip Whalen discusses the American language as a system distinct from English. He focuses on poems of Wallace Stevens, particularly "The Bed of Old John Zoeller" and also discusses H.L. Mencken, Lew Welch, and his own family history. (Continues on 80p094.) Keywords: New American Poetry, West Coast poetry, Buddhism, American modernist poetry, symbolism
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: In the pressure tank, Class 1

docs.creator: Brownstein, Michael
docs.description: Second half of the first meeting of a class on "Investigative poetics," including discussions on Gregory Corso, Ed Sanders, cut-ups, underground science,Timothy Leary, General Electric light bulbs, IBM, and imagery. (Continued from 77p035.)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Michael Brownstein class, "Investigative poetics."

docs.creator: Whalen, Philip
docs.description: Second half of Class 9 of "In the Pressure Tank" series held at Naropa Institute between July 23 and August 20, 1980. (The whole series is contained on 80P093-115.) Philip Whalen discusses Hart Crane's life during the period in which "The Bridge" was composed, with an emphasis on the literary climate of the time. (Continued from 80p107.) Keywords: New American Poetry, West Coast poetry, Buddhism, American modernist poetry, symbolism
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: In the pressure tank, Class 9

docs.creator: Brown, Lee Ann; Delany, Samuel R.; du Plessis, Michael;
docs.description: Conclusion of Panen on Feminism and Gender with questions on cinema, pronouns and children's literature. This is part 2 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Feminism and Gender panel part 2 June 2002

docs.creator: Augustine, Jane
docs.description: First half of a Jane Augustine class. Augustine lectures on feminist studies, focusing on Clarise Lispector. Other topics include the avant-garde and the ego, the penis, and the French feminists. (Continues on 90P076)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Jane Augustine class, Clarice Lispector, July, 1990.

docs.creator: Corso, Gregory
docs.description: Class instructed by Gregory Corso entitled Poetry the Container. The class includes Corso reading his works City Child's Day and Mortal Infliction and discussion of student work. This is workshop 1 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Gregory Corso workshop 1 July 1981

docs.creator: Coolidge, Clark; Creeley, Robert; Tallman, Warren
docs.description: Robert Creeley, Warren Tallman, and Clark Coolidge discuss Kerouac's works, including Dr. Sax, Visions of Cody, On the road, Lonesome traveler, and Old angel midnight. At the end, the panel takes questions from the audience.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Kerouac Conference Symposium June 1982

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Tape 3 in an 11 tape series of a class taught by Allen Ginsberg on Expansive Poetics. Subject matter includes some discussion of the Russian Futurists and two short readings by Russian Futurist writers.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Class 3 Expansive Poetics July 1981

docs.creator: Rosenthal, Bob
docs.description: A Bob Rosenthal class. He discusses his development and influences as a writer, and reads from his work, Cleaning Up New York and "Fifth Avenue overhead."
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Bob Rosenthal class, True reality fiction, August, 1980.

docs.creator: Hawkins, Bobbie Louise
docs.description: A writing class by Bobbie Louise Hawkins from 1978 at Naropa Institute. In this class Bobbie explore an interdisciplinary approach to pedigogy following the motto, "Education is teaching someone how to learn for the rest of their lives." In this Bobbie does not discuss writing explicitly, but rather reads from various works, both literary and critical to create an atmosphere of indipendant exploration in learning. This is class 1 of 3.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Bobbie Hawkins class 1 August 1978

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: The second tape in a two tape series covering political poetics and the Russian poets. Also included are readings of the work of Pablo Neruda and the conept of imagination and emotional breakthrough.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg lecture political poetics part 12July 1989

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: First half of an Anne Waldman class, continuing her series from the summer of 1977 on women writers, focusing on Virginia Woolf. She begins by reading invocations written by students, then reads and discusses selections from Woolf's work, including "To the lighthouse" and "Mrs. Dalloway." The class concludes with a question and answer session. (Continued on 77P076)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman class, Women writers, August, 1977.

docs.creator: Burke, Junior; Bye, Reed; Coultas, Brenda; Hunt, Laird; Rugenstein, Laurie; Taylor, Steven
docs.description: A reading from June of 2003. Performers on this tape are Brenda Coultas and Reed Bye with Steven Taylor, Junior Burke, and Laurie Rugenstein. Coultas reads from her book "The Bowery Project." Bye's band plays three songs including "Imagination Gets Real." This is part 2 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Faculty Reading with Coultas, Bye, Burke, Guravich part 2 June 2003

docs.creator: Blaser, Robin
docs.description: A reading (tape 2 of 2) held at Naropa University June 6 2003. Robin Blaser concludes the evening of readers that included Elizabeth Robinson and Kenneth Irby. Blaser reads from his books The Holy Forest and Wonders as well as newer work. This is part 2 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Faculty reading with Hawkins, Blaser part 2 June 2003

docs.creator: Burroughs, William S.; Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Allen Ginsberg class with William Burroughs. Ginsberg begins by reading from Burroughs's work, including his book Nova Express. Burroughs arrives and discusses writing techniques, including the idea that "Life is a cut up." He also talks about why he became a writer, Laurie Anderson, rolling drunks, biological warfare, weapons and retreats. The class learns some exercises for observing details while walking down the street.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg and William Burroughs class, July, 1984.

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: An Anne Waldman class, "Poet as Shaman," part 6. Waldman lectures on the work of Jack Spicer, Robert Duncan and John Ashbery. Waldman also discusses dream analysis. (Series continues on 79P036)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman class, Poet as shaman, part 6, July, 1979.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: This is the 3rd session of a class in basic poetics taught by Allen Ginsberg in 1980 at the Naropa Institute. In this class, Ginsberg discusses H. Phelps Putnam, and reads Putnam's Hasbrook and the rose. He then reads and discusses Geoffrey Chaucer's Merciless beauty in conjunction with Ezra Pound's Cantos 81. After discussing alliteration and other aspects of verse, he reads and discusses Pound's translation of The sea-farer. He reads three different versions of Langland's Piers Plowman, and ends the class with reading and discussing W. H. Auden's Age of anxiety. This is class 3 of 33.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Basic Poetics, Class 3

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: First half of an Allen Ginsberg class on writing poetry. He begins by referring to William Carlos Williams's exhortation, "No ideas but in things," comparing it to Chogyam Trungpa Rinpoche's statement that "Things are symbols of themselves." He reads from Shakespeare's poetry to illustrate his point. During the lecture, Ginsberg also touches on Haiku, Kerouac, and other topics. (Continued on 84P023)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class, On writing poetry, July, 1984.

docs.creator: Burroughs, William S.; Giorno, John
docs.description: Second half of a William S. Burroughs, Sr. and William S. Burroughs, Jr. reading, with John Giorno. William S. Burroughs finishes his reading from The Gay Gun. Buddhist poet Giorno reads two energetic long poems "Eating the sky," and "Put your ear to stone and open your heart to the sky." The latter presentation is accompanied by a recording of Giorno reading the piece earlier, with the sound effect of a distorted, repeating echo. (Continued from 79P103)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: William S. Burroughs Sr. and John Giorno reading, August, 1979.

docs.creator: Whalen, Philip
docs.description: First half of a class with Philip Whalen discussing Alexander Pope's life, and the cultural context of his work. Whalen reads and discusses several works by Pope, including "The Heathen to His Departing Soul," "The Dying Christian to His Soul," "A Rondeau," "An Epistle to a Doctor ofDivinity...," and "The Dunciad." (Continues on 84p043.) Keywords: New American Poetry, West Coast poetry, Buddhism, 17th and 18th century literatur.
docs.title: Philip Whalen class on Alexander Pope - Part 1

docs.creator: Creeley, Robert
docs.description: First half of a Robert Creeley lecture on eco-poetics. Creeley discusses Edwin Arlington Robinson, Marsden Hartley, Creeley's time in the American Field Service, existentialism, Jack Kerouac and the dignity of being a writer, Hart Crane, Robert Frost and Louis Zukofsky. Creeley recounts stories from his own life and talks about the ways in which Robinson influenced him. During the course of the lecture Creeley reads his own tribute to Robinson, "Old poems," as well as part of Robinson's "The man against the sky." He also reads and discusses the work of Hart Crane and other writers. (Continues on 97P005)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Robert Creeley lecture on eco-poetics, part 1, June, 1997.

docs.creator: Hawkins, Bobbie Louise; Jones, Hettie; Vega, Janine Pommy
docs.description: Summer Writing Program faculty reading from 2000. Bobby Louise Hawkins reads from what she describes as a novel in progress tentatively titled Welcome to the Bon Voyage Hotel. Janine Pommy Vega reads from her book of poems The Mad Dogs of Trieste. Hettie Jones reads several of her own poems.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Reading with Hawkins, Vega, Jones June 2000

docs.creator: Whalen, Philip
docs.description: The second half of a class by Philip Whalen at Naropa Univesity from August 1977 about classic literature. Works such as Uncle Tom's Cabin, and Ben Hur are discussed. Also presented are modernizations and the missing of genuine feeling in Shakespeare productions. (Continued from 77P027)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Philip Whalen class, part 2, August 1977.

docs.creator: Wilson, Peter Lamborn
docs.description: A Peter Lamborn Wilson lecture on utopian communities in America, including a 17th century community of mystics founded by Johannes Kelpius and known as The Society of the Woman in the Wilderness. Wilson divides communities into two types: platonic (based on an authoritarian, usually Christian, ideology) and anti-platonic (based on autonomy and equality). He evaluates communities according to how they perceive nature and wilderness, putting his discussion in the context of the differences in outlook between the indigenous peoples of America and the European colonists, and focusing on those colonists who joined Indian communities or incorporated native ideas and customs into their way of life. Wilson concludes by playing some hymns by Johannes Kelpius.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Peter Lamborn Wilson lecture, Woman in the wilderness, July, 1993.

docs.creator: David Cope
docs.description: David Cope talks about imagist and objectivist poetry. He reads several of his poems including "Baseball" and "The Stars". He and Allen Ginsberg dialogue about some other poets. Resnikov, Hartley, etc. Gergory Corso tells a story about Trungpa Rinpoche continues on 80P125. This class is part 4 of 4.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: David Cope, part 4 July 1980

docs.creator: Brownstein, Michael
docs.description: First half of the first meeting of a class on "Investigative poetics," including discussions on William Blake, Fascism, autocrats, and current politics. (Continued on 77p036.)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Michael Brownstein class - Part 1

docs.creator: Creeley, Robert
docs.description: Second half of a lecture by Robert Creeley discussing family relations, the Tibetan Book of the Dead, Ted Berrigan, Charles Olson and syntax, Cole's Island, and Ginsberg's "Laughing Gas." (First half of this lecture is currently not available.)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Robert Creeley lecture - Part 2

docs.creator: Padgett, Ron
docs.description: First half of a class by Ron Padgett on writing poetry. He separates poetry into two types, that with a plan and that without. He discusses acrostics (a Victorian parlor game), "I remember," and other writing exercises. (Continues on 75p029). Keywords: New American Poetry, New York School
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Ron Padgett class on writing poetry - Part 1

docs.creator: Padgett, Ron
docs.description: Second half of a class by Ron Padgett on writing poetry. He separates poetry into two types, that with a plan and that without. He discusses acrostics (a Victorian parlor game), "I remember," and other writing exercises. (Continued from 75p298) Keywords: New American Poetry, New York School
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Ron Padgett class on writing poetry - Part 2

docs.creator: Codrescu, Andrei
docs.description: A lecture bu Andrei Codrescu speaking about his experiences in Romania with National Public Radio during the Romanian revolution. Keywords: New American Poetry, New York School, society and literature, protest poetry
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: The state of Romania.

docs.creator: Coolidge, Clark; Creeley, Robert; Hawkins, Bobbie Louise; Hollo, Anselm
docs.description: A reading at the Boulder Theater by Clark Coolidge and Robert Creeley with introductions by Bobbie Louise Hawkins and Anselm Hollo. The readings include Coolidge's "City in Regard" and Creeley's "So There," "O Max," "Life," "Helsinki Window," "The Seasons" and "Body." (Continues on 91p071.)

docs.creator: Brown, Lee Ann

docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Lee Ann Brown workshop July 1991

docs.creator: Elmslie, Kenward; Taylor, Steven
docs.description: Kenward Elmslie and Steven Taylor lecture about writing lyrics and melodies to songs, focusing on their Palais bimbo lounge show album. Elmslie begins with a writing assignment for the class which is a poem in itself. He goes on to talk about how he started writing melodies when he worked as a lyricist. Elmslie reads "At the controls," from his book Tropicalism and talks about how it became a song called "Eggs." Taylor plays the orchestration and sings the song. They also perform and discuss other songs and poems including "Meat," "Sneaky Pete," "And I was there," "26 bars," and "Quarks report." Elmslie also plays a recording of a scene from the opera "The seagull" by Thomas Pasatieri. The last portion of the tape is a question and answer period.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Kenward Elmslie and Steven Taylor lecture, Palais bimbo, July, 1991.

docs.creator: Mullen, Harryette
docs.description: A Harryette Mullen lecture from the 2002 Naropa Summer Writing Program. Mullen discusses her interest in dictionaries, language and its reflection of human social dynamics. She also reads from and discusses an interview with her by Daniel Kane. They discuss the creation of her book Muse and Drudge, and discuss questions of race and gender in writing. She also touches on issues of language, colonization, identity, and writing tools such as Oulipo exercises.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Harryette Mullen lecture on language, June, 2002.

docs.creator: Joris, Pierre
docs.description: Part 4 of a four part workshop with Pierre Joris, with students reading assigned 24-hour journal poems. Discussions range from editing, line breaks and moving throughout the space-time continuum. (Continued from 96P042)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Pierre Joris workshop, Poems for the millennium, part 4, July, 1996.

docs.creator: Carroll, Jim
docs.description: Second half of the second installment of Jim Carroll's class on poetry and music. Carroll plays recordings of his songs and discusses his music, including a collaboration with Ray Manzerik of the Doors. The tape ends with a performance by the class. (Continued from 86P005)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Jim Carroll class, Poetics and music, June, 1986.

docs.creator: Hejinian, Lyn
docs.description: A workshop taught by Lyn Hejinian at the Naropa Institute July 6, 1992. Hejinian begins the class by discussing the work and person of Gertrude Stein. She then speaks a bit about Russian Formalism and ends the class by inviting her students to read their poems.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Lyn Hejinian workshop part 1 July 1992

docs.creator: Hejinian, Lyn
docs.description: A workshop taught by Lyn Hejinian at the Naropa Institute July 9, 1992. Hejinian spends most of the class discussing the work of Francis Ponge, Clark Coolidge and Steve Benson. The class ends with students reading their workshop assignments.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Lyn Hejinian workshop part 2 July 1992

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Allen Ginsberg class on Beat literary history of the 1950's discussing student sketches, the first manuscript of "Howl," and Burroughs's early work including The Yage Letters and "Roosevelt after inauguration." Part 17 of a 20 part series.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class, Literary history of the Beat generation, the 50's, part 17, May, 1981.

docs.creator: Retallack, Joan
docs.description: Joan Retallack lecture discussing Gertrude Stein's influence on John Cage. The correlations between Stein and Cage are related to their style of writing and the avante-garde. Retallack discusses the necessity of coincidence, surprise, and crime in the world and in writing, and that real time cannot be mirrored in literature or performance. This form of writing is contrasted with conventional writing styles.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Joan Retallack lecture, Geometries of attention, Cage's silence, July, 2002.

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne
docs.description: Second half of a poetry reading with Jena Osman, Bob Perelman, Mei Mei Bersenbrugge, and Joanne Kyger. Kyger reads from her book, Again. (Continued from 00P025)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Jena Osman, Bob Perelman, Mei Mei Bersenbrugge, and Joanne Kyger reading, June, 2001.

docs.creator: Augustine, Jane
docs.description: A Jane Augustine class discussing the connections between imagism and objectivism, HD's life, and the similarities between HD and Lorine Niedecker's writing.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Jane Augustine class, Imagism, objectivism, and feminism, July, 1987.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Second half of Part 3 of an Allen Ginsberg workshop on American value. Ginsberg reads several poems as examples of the mind in operation and talks about how poetry can arise from meditation practice and ordinary mind. He reads and discusses the work of Charles Reznikoff, William Carlos Williams, and other writers. (Continued from 87P083)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class, American value, part 3, March, 1987.

docs.creator: Kapil Rider, Bhanu; Patton, Julie; Schelling, Andrew
docs.description: Second half of a faculty reading with Julie Patton, Banu Kapil, and Andrew Schelling. Patton reads "Flower poem." and others. (Continued from 01P101)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Banu Kapil, Julie Patten, Andrew Schelling reading, July, 2001.

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: First half of an Anne Waldman workshop on writing. The class begins with a discussion about what led people to come to the Kerouac conference. Waldman talks about how she became involved with the Beats and came to Boulder, the founding of Naropa, and Kerouac's influence on the school. She reads and discusses part of an interview with William Carlos Williams, about writing poetry, and selections from Gertrude Stein, Vladimir Mayakovsky, and other poets. Students read their work and Waldman comments and makes suggestions. (Continues on 82P317B)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman workshop, Kerouac conference, June, 1982.

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: First half of the final class from Anne Waldman's month-long series on female writers, "Some Women Writers," during the summer of 1977. Waldman continues the discussion about Gertrude Stein that began in the August 15th class. She reads excerpts from Stein's book Lifting Belly, "A piece of coffee" from Stein's book Tender Buttons, followed by Stein's comments on "A piece of coffee." Waldman also reads some of Clark Coolidge's work and compares it to that of Stein. The final part of the class is devoted to student presentations. (Continued on 77P084)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman class on poetics and female writers, August, 1977.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Allen Ginsberg subtitutes for a workshop class taught by Tom Pickard recorded April 1, 1981 at Naropa. In this class, Allen discusses poetic composition using Corso, Marshall,Spicer, Kerouac, Blake, Pound, Williams, Bunting and others as examples. Later, students present their work and Ginsberg gives critiques often discussing the methods of composition, structureing, and selection of vocabulary in poetry. Continued on 81P110
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Workshop part 1 April 1981

docs.creator: Burroughs, William S.
docs.description: Second half of a class with William S. Burroughs, continuing with his exploration of egoless sources for writing, focusing on the nature of egolessness, especially its relation to Buddhist notions of egolessness and nonattachment. Notably, Burroughs maintains that "the goal of enlightenment is not necessarily the goal of the writer." There are some brief digressions on the relation between written, spoken, and nonverbal communication. (Continued from 76p020. Continues on 76p022.) Keywords: Beat Movement, Experimental Writing, Aural Poetry, Consciousness and Literature

docs.creator: Burroughs, William S.
docs.description: First half of a William S. Burroughs lecture on creative reading. The lecture mentions a wide variety of authors, including Alistair Crowley, Paul Bowles, and many others. The class also discusses science fiction, non-fiction, general semantics, scriptwriting, cloning, rotten ectoplasm, and judgment in cut-ups, as well as Burroughs's novel, The Soft Machine. (Continues on 79p044.) Keywords: beat movement, experimental literature, consciousness in literature, reality mapping
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: William S. Burroughs class on creative reading - Part 1

docs.creator: Burroughs, William S.
docs.description: First half of a workshop with William S. Burroughs comparing his works to those of Jack Kerouac, discussing their writing techniques. Burroughs provides biographical information on where the two met and their relationship. He also discusses what it means to be a writer and how many people are not writers even though they claim to be and have published work. Burroughs responds to questions about his relationship with Kerouac, dreams, and his own literary influences. This workshop took place during the 1982 Jack Kerouac Conference at the Naropa Institute.(Continues on 82p267B.) Keywords: beat movement, history of beat movement, 20th century literature
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: William S. Burroughs workshop, Jack Kerouac Conference - Part 1

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: First half of an Allen Ginsberg survey class on historical poetics. Ginsberg discusses topics, styles, and modes that he found useful in his own poetry, and that every poet should know. He includes a discussion of preliterate traditions; quantitative verse, including classic meters and long and short vowels; sonnets; song forms; and a discussion of poetry expressing states of consciousness. He shows how older forms are still alive in the work of contemporary poets, using as examples the works of Pound, Melville, Blake, Auden, Kerouac, Poe, Bob Dylan, and others. (Continues on 92P056)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class, Pound, Wordsworth, and Poe, July, 1992.

docs.creator: Warsh, Lewis
docs.description: a continuation of a Visiting Poets class conducted by Lewis Warsh in 1978 (78P073 side two) covering autobiographical writing of prose and poetry, how the writer makes it into writing. In this class he focuses on letters and journals as a way to generate material for writing and as writing. This is part 3 of 3.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Lewis Warsh class June 1978

docs.creator: Rothenberg, Jerome
docs.description: First half of a Jerome Rothenberg class on ethnopoetics and performance, discussing shamanism, performance as ritual, gaining knowledge through experience, meditation, Seneca songs, being prisoners of language, trance and illusionism. Part 4 of a series. (Continued on 81P022B)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Jerome Rothenberg class on ethnopoetics and performance, August, 1981, part 4.

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne
docs.description: A workshop, "Beat And Other Rebel Angel," taught by Joanne Kyger at the Naropa Institute October 1991. Kyger continues speaking about and discussing the work of the poet Jack Spicer focusing on Spicer's book "Admonitions."
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Joanne Kyger beat rebel angels class 2 October 1991

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne
docs.description: This is the second class in a series given by Joanne Kyger at the Naropa Institute in 1981 entitled Compassion for Place. Kyger looks heavily into Native American storytelling and poetry, focusing mainly on the plethora of Coyote Stories that are told in many different traditions, including here the Achomawi and Okanagan, and also on the works of native poets Jaime de Angulo and Simon Ortiz. This is class 1 of 12.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Joanne Kyger class 1 part 1 June 1981

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne
docs.description: Kyger has the class read the work they wrote in reponse to assignments on the coyote story and compassion for place. She also lectures on Maria Sabina and reads some of her work. This is class 7 of 12.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Joanne Kyger class 7 June 1981

docs.creator: Hamill, Sam; Kyger, Joanne; Rodney, Janet; Schelling, Andrew; Warshall, Peter
docs.description: A panel on dharma and eco-poetics with Janet Rodney, Sam Hamill, Joanne Kyger, and Peter Warshall, chaired by Andrew Schelling. The panel discusses the information age; busy-ness and doing nothing; the ecology of paper production; nature, and conscientious objection to overpopulation and capitalism; English language nature writing; and the disconnection from nature in English language poetry. A question and answer period concludes the panel.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Peter Warshall, Sam Hamill, Janet Rodney, Joanne Kyger, and Andrew Schelling panel, June, 1995.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Part 1 of an Allen Ginsberg workshop on American value. Ginsberg looks at what a value is, what is of value, and at poetry that addresses these questions. He focuses on the work of artist and poet Marsden Hartley, reading and discussing his poems, including "Three small feathers," "As the buck lay dead," "Albert Ryder, moonlightist," and others. Ginsberg also touches on the work of William Carlos Williams and Ezra Pound.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class, American value, part 1, March, 1987.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Allen Ginsberg lecture on poetry, reading and discussing the lyrics to some of Bob Dylan's songs, talking about how to arrange lines of poetry on a page, and how phrasing relates to ideas and breath. Ginsberg looks at his own poem, "Wichita vortex sutra," and touches on the work of William Carlos Williams, Gregory Corso, and Kurt Schwitters's Concrete poetry. Part of a course series by Ginsberg in fall 1983.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class, Poetics IV, November, 1983.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: A literature class, "Basic Poetics," taught by Allen Ginsberg at The Naropa Institute April 28, 1980. The majority of the class is spent reading and discussing the work of the poets John Suckling and Andrew Marvell. The work of Anne Bradstreet, Abraham Cowley, Richard Crawshaw, Thomas Carew, and Richard Lovelace is also discussed. This is class 26 of 33.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Basic Poetics, Class 26

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: A literature class, "Basic Poetics," taught by Allen Ginsberg at The Naropa Institute May 22, 1980. Ginsberg spends the class reading and discussing the work of various poets throughout the ages who have dealt with the Sapphic form, from the ancient Greeks to Ezra Pound. Included are a number of different translations of works by Catullus. Ginsberg also plays recordings of Ed Sanders reciting poems by Sappho and Blake. This is class 31 of 33.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Basic Poetics class 31

docs.creator: Osman, Jena

docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Jena Osman lecture, Cog-ignitions, June, 2001.

docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Carl Rakosi part 1 June 1989

docs.creator: Cage, John

docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: John Cage interview and performance, Empty words, August, 1974.
