docs.creator: Creeley, Robert
docs.description: A lecture by Robert Creeley on poetry in motion. The lecture includes a discussion and reading of Basil Bunting, playing of jazz, and selections from Poetry in Motion by Amiri Baraka, Anne Waldman, Kenward Elsmslie, Ed Sanders, Helen Adam, Tom Waits, William S. Burroughs, and Michael McClure. Keywords: New American Poetry, objectivist poetry, Black Mountain School, art in literature, music in literature, San Francisco Renaissance, modernism
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Robert Creeley lecture on poetry in motion.

docs.creator: Creeley, Robert; Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Second half of a lecture by Robert Creeley on the imagination of procedure with advice on Ezra Pound, William Carlos Williams, Robert Duncan, Walt Whitman, Hart Crane, Robert Frost, and Louis Zukofsky. Also included in this lecture are readings from Pound, Whitman, and Creeley's own works. Allen Ginsberg adds to the lecture by posing a specific question to Creeley about Whitman and Charles Olson. (Continued from 86p021.) Keywords: New American Poetry, objectivist poetry, Black Mountain School, art in literature, music in literature, San Francisco Renaissance, modernism
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Robert Creeley lecture on the imagination of procedure - Part 2

docs.creator: Gladman, Renee; Kyger, Joanne; Mullen, Harryette; Sikelianos, Eleni; Taylor, Steven; Waldman, Anne
docs.description: First half of a panel with Anne Waldman, Joanne Kyger, Eleni Sikelianos, Harryette Mullen, Steven Taylor, and Renee Gladman. Waldman reads "Sister arise and vocalize: is there anyone under that chador?" Kyger discusses modernist women poets. Sikelianos reads "Yo, self / yo, maximus." Mullen discusses categories, forms, and perceptions. Taylor discusses Claude Levi-Strauss, Simone de Beauvoir, Julia Kristeva. Renee Gladman discusses poetry and triangles. (Continues on 02P032)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman, Joanne Kyger, Eleni Sikelianos, Harryette Mullen, Steven Taylor, Renee Gladman panel, June, 2002.

docs.creator: Dorn, Ed
docs.description: This is the first class in a series taught by Ed Dorn in the summer of 1977. In this class the works of Edward Abbey are contrasted with JB Jackson's. Also a History of the Mayans and Aztecs are given with selection read from Aztec writing. The class continues on the next tape 7P006. This is part 1 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Ed Dorn class part 1 June 1977

docs.creator: Ed Dorn
docs.description: This is the second class in a series taught by Ed Dorn in the summer of 1977. Disscussion and reading of "Gunslinger" Influences on "Gunslinger" Continued discussion and reading of "Gunslinger" Dorn's early experiences in the West. The Drive-away car life and being on the road, pre-Jack Kerouac. Writing "Gunslinger". This is part 2 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.subject: Ed Dorn
docs.title: Ed_Dorn_class_part_22_June_1977_77P004

docs.creator: Dorn, Ed
docs.description: This is the second class in a series taught by Ed Dorn in the summer of 1977. Disscussion and reading of "Gunslinger" Influences on "Gunslinger" Continued discussion and reading of "Gunslinger" Dorn's early experiences in the West. The Dive-away car life and being on the road, pre-Jack Kerouac. Writing "Gunslinger". This is part 1 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Ed Dorn class part 2 June 1977

docs.creator: Myles, Eileen; Pate, Alexs
docs.description: Eileen Myles and Alexs Pate lecture about art, culture and politics. Myles discusses relating to the mainstream as an outsider by creating art that engages the community. Pate talks about his experience as a black man with racial hierarchy, Halloween, innocence and guilt. He compares rap music to the news station CNN as a way of finding out what's going on. An open discussion with the audience covers a wide range of topics relating to diversity. (Continued from 01P053)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Eileen Myles and Alexs Pate lecture, Hip hop culture, June, 2001.

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne
docs.description: In this class Kyger finishes discussing Burroughs, and students read their papers. Kyger reads Burroughs' poem Thanksgiving Day 11-28-86. John Weiners is introduced with a detailed biography on him and his growing mental illness. Two poems from his Hotel Wentley collection, Poem for record players and Poem for painters, are read aloud by students. Kyger then gives a detailed biography of Bob Kaufman, and reads All those ships that never sailed from his book Ancient rain '56-'76. She also mentions Raymond Foye, who compiled the work of and wrote biographies about both Weiners and Kaufman. Kyger reads a postcard she recently received from John Montgomery, and Kaufman's Blood fell on the mountains.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Joanne Kyger beat rebel angels class 9 November 1991

docs.creator: Cage, John
docs.description: A John Cage studio reading of "Mureau", "She's asleep", and "Six melodies for violin and keyboard."
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: John Cage studio performance, January, 1979.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Ginsberg class on Emily Dickinson and Gregory Corso. He talks about the recent invasion of Grenada by the United States, then improvises a poem about the invasion and discusses it. Ginsberg talks about the poetry of Gregory Corso and Emily Dickinson and the connection between the two. He reads Dickinson's "Before I got my eye put out" and "A bird came down to the walk."
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class on Emily Dickinson and Gregory Corso, November, 1983.

docs.creator: McMorris, Mark; Nguyen, Hoa; Palmer, Michael
docs.description: First half of a Summer Writing Program faculty reading with Hoa Nguyen, Mark McMorriss and Michael Palmer. Each writer reads a selection of their work, including "The Trang sisters" by Nguyen, "A Poem for the love of women" by McMorris," and "Sun" by Michael Palmer. (Continues on 02P014)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Michael Palmer, Hoa Nguyen, Mark McMorris reading, June, 2002.

docs.creator: Monk, Meredith
docs.description: Meredith Monk, composer, singer, director, choreographer, performs Our Lady of Late. Monk's vocals are accompanied by wine glass and percussion.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Meredith Monk performance, July, 1975.

docs.creator: Randall, Margaret
docs.description: This is the third tape of a workshop with Margaret Randall. The students express their feelings and views regarding activism in Latin American countries. Margaret talks mainly about collective memory and the power of creation as writers. She mentions her time in Uruguay and Nicaraguan Sandanistas. Related tapes 90P063, 90P064, 90P066
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Margaret Randall Workshop part 1 July 1990

docs.creator: Randall, Margaret; Zamora, Daisy
docs.description: Margaret Randall Workshop continued from 90P065 which discsusses the idea of separating the dichotomy in political action. She mentions Ruth Hubbard's "The Politics of Women's Biology" and how the environment is not a split cause, but a global one that adjoins to politics. Daisy Zamora then talks to the class about the ongoing struggle in Nicaragua under Violeta Chamorro and the Agency of International Development and the involvement of the United States.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Margaret Randall Workshop part 2 July 1990

docs.creator: Perloff, Marjorie
docs.description: Marjorie Perloff lectures on Allen Ginsberg and the poetics of everyday life. Perloff traces the influence of Ludwig Wittgenstein's work on the arts of the 20th Century, and discusses Marianne Moore's reactions to Ginsberg's early work in relation to Wittgenstein's concern with the uses of language in everyday life.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Majorie Perloff lecture, Allen Ginsberg and the poetics of everyday life, July, 1994.

docs.creator: Palmer, Michael
docs.description: Second half of a Summer Writing Program faculty reading with Hoa Nguyen, Mark McMorriss and Michael Palmer. Palmer reads "The metaphysician of Prague, autobiography 11" and "Burning deck," among others.(Continued from 02P013)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Michael Palmer, Hoa Nguyen, Mark McMorris reading, June, 2002.

docs.creator: diPrima, Diane
docs.description: A Diane di Prima reading, accompanied by Art Landy. Di Prima reads poems that span her career until that point, including "Loba" poems.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Diane di Prima reading July 1987

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Allen Ginsberg class on steps of revising autobiographical poems. The class includes readings of Hart Crane and Percy Shelley and discussions about Gregory Corso, Basil Bunting, and Ezra Pound. The class also includes discussions and reviews of student work.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
subject: New American Poetry
modernist poetry
romantic poetry
autobiography
beat movement
objectivist
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class on revising autobiographical poems.

docs.creator: Schelling, Andrew
docs.description: Wrap up of a class by Andrew Schelling focusing on crisis cults, protest songs as healing songs, songs with meaningless language, an Anne Waldman abortion poem, the poet as witness, Anna Akmanava poems, epic travel poems, activism and letter writing. (Continued from 90p003.)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
subject: New American Poetry
political poetry
docs.title: Andrew Schelling class on activism and writing - Part 2

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: Second half of a class from Anne Waldman's month-long series on female writers, "Some Women Writers," during the summer of 1977. This class is about Emily Dickinson. Her life and work are discusssed in great detail. Anne reads Dickinson's work and offers information on Dickinson's biography, poetry, and letters. (Continued from 77p068.)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
subject: New American Poetry
New York School
women poets
feminist poetry
spiritualism and literature
docs.title: Anne Waldman class on poetics and female writers - Part 2

docs.creator: Campbell, Duncan; diPrima, Diane; Ginsberg, Allen; Giorno, John; Trungpa Rinpoche, Chogyam; Waldman, Anne
docs.description: A lecture and reading with Chogyam Trungpa Rinpoche, Allen Ginsberg, Anne Waldman, Diane diPrima and John Giorno. The talks include Trungpa Rinpoche on Tibetan poetry, fundamental craziness, how to be a poet, and an exerpt of a Trungpa Rinpoche question and answer session. The readings include Trungpa Rinpoche's "Cynical Letter," Ginsberg's "Energy Vampire," Waldman's "Fast Speaking Woman," diPrima's "Ave," and Giorno's "Suicide Sutra." The event ends with a spontaneous talking poem by everyone. Keywords: New American Poetry, beat movement, New York School, performance poetry, Buddhism
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Art of poetry reading at the Naropa Institute.

docs.creator: Creeley, Robert
docs.description: Second half of a lecture by Robert Creeley discussing John Weiners and his poems "A Poem for Painters," "A Poem for the Insane," and "A Poem for Trapped Things," affect vs. effect, Charles Olsen, San Francisco in 1956, his works "My Mother" and "An Anniversary of Death," William S. Burroughs, and Dogtown. (Continued from 86p017.) Keywords: New American Poetry, objectivist poetry, Black Mountain School, art in literature, music in literature, San Francisco Renaissance, modernism
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Robert Creeley lecture on John Weiners and his poems - Part 2

docs.creator: Burroughs, William S.
docs.description: William S. Burroughs lectures on creative reading, including a discussion about various authors including Joseph Conrad, Denton Welch, Jane Bowles, Brion Gysin, and Julian Jaynes. Burroughs also addresses subjects such as art heroes, hemispheres of the brain, and the training of assasins. Keywords: beat movement, experimental literature, consciousness in literature
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: William S. Burroughs class on creative reading

docs.creator: Burroughs, William S.
docs.description: Second half of a William S. Burroughs lecture on creative reading. The lecture mentions a wide variety of authors, including Alistair Crowley, Paul Bowles, and many others. The class also discusses science fiction, non-fiction, general semantics, scriptwriting, cloning, rotten ectoplasm, and judgment in cut-ups, as well as Burroughs's novel, The Soft Machine. (Continued from 79p043.) Keywords: beat movement, experimental literature, consciousness in literature, reality mapping
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: William S. Burroughs class on creative reading - Part 2

docs.creator: Smith, Harry
docs.description: Harry Smith shows his films while playing various musical selections to accompany them.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
subject: mysticism
consciousness
docs.title: Harry Smith lecture

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne
docs.description: A lecture with Joanne Kyger discussing Native American folklore and folklorists, focusing on stories from her native California.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
subject: New American Poetry
West Coast poetry
ecopoetics
docs.title: Joanne Kyger lecture on the poet as historical investigator.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen; McClure, Michael
docs.description: A "Visiting poetics" class by Michael McClure in June, 1976. McClure teaches "word deck exercises" and gives the class an assignment involving William Blake's song "The tyger." A class discussion about the exercises follows.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Michael McClure and Allen Ginsberg class, Card games, June, 1976.

docs.creator: McClure, Michael
docs.description: First half of a Michael McClure lecture about the origins of theater. He discusses the relationship between plays and poetry, his concept of "beast language" and his own plays, "The feast," "The beard" and "Josephine the mouse singer." (Continues on 89P134)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Michael McClure lecture about the origins of theater, July, 1989.

docs.creator: Roark, Randy
docs.description: Randy Roark talks about William Butler Yeats as part of Tom Pickard's class on Basil Bunting. Roark discusses Yeats's life and touches on connections between Yeats, Bunting, and Ezra Pound. He reads Yeats's work, including "A coat" and "The fisherman." Pickard adds comments and answers questions.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Randy Roarke lecture on William Butler Yeats, May, 1981.

docs.creator: Charters, Sam
docs.description: Sam Charters lecture on Jack Kerouac and jazz at the Jack Kerouac conference, sponsored by the Naropa Institute in Boulder, Colorado. The lecture includes discussions on jazz of the Beat generation, be-bop, Thelonius Monk, Dizzy Gillespie, Charlie Parker, and a recording of Kerouac and Steve Allen reading "Mexico City blues."
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: On the road: The Jack Kerouac conference, Sam Charters lecture, Jack and jazz, July, 1982.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: First half of an Allen Ginsberg workshop for On the road: The Jack Kerouac conference, sponsored by the Naropa Institute. Ginsberg discusses word choices, vividness, juxtaposition, sound, epics, the concept of "first thought, best thought" and Buddhism. (Continues on 82P316B)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: On the road: The Jack Kerouac conference, Allen Ginsberg workshop, July, 1982.

docs.creator: Creeley, Robert
docs.description: Second half of Robert Creeley lecture on eco-poetics discussing George Herbert and reading "Signs," "Echo's arrow," "Old poems," "Mitch," "Life and death," "Inside my head," "The swan," "The rose" and "The star." (Continued from 97P004)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Robert Creeley lecture on eco-poetics, June, 1997.

docs.creator: Blaser, Robin
docs.description: A lecture given by Robin Blaser June 27, 2001. Blaser spends the majority of the lecture speaking about what her terms "cultural despair." He also discusses at length the practive and process of writing his libretto. After his lecture the floor is opened up for Q & A. This is part 1 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Robin Blaser lecture part 1 June 2001

docs.creator: Corso, Gregory
docs.description: Gregory Corso presents a class on the Sumerian Gilgamesh epic, discussing the historical background of the epic, Gilgamesh as a tragic seeker, the goddess Tiamat, the relationship of Enkidu to Gilgamesh and the animal world, and immortality and impermanence.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Gregory Corso class 1 July 1977

docs.creator: Kapil Rider, Bhanu; Owen, Maureen; Patton, Julie; Schelling, Andrew
docs.description: First half of a faculty reading with Banu Kapil, Julie Patten, Andrew Schelling, Steve Lacy, and Maureen Owen. Schelling reads "Crossing the seas of Saint Brendan," "Sing's chair", and "The spiral path." Lacy accompanies Schelling in performing translations of classical Indian poetry. (Continues on 01P102).
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Banu Kapil, Julie Patten, Andrew Schelling, Maureen Owen reading, July, 2001.

docs.creator: Dorn, Ed
docs.description: Ed Dorn finishes his reading with "Period Westerns" and "An Opinion on a Matter of Public Safety."
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Ed Dorn reads poem October 1977

docs.creator: Hawkins, Bobbie Louise
docs.description: A Bobbie Louise Hawkins lecture, The sounding word. Hawkins discusses the writings of Werner Heisenberg and his uncertainty principle, Louis Zukofsky on defining poetry, Ysaye Barnwell's views of the effect of singing on the physical human body, Paul Valery, Michael Ondaatje from his book Coming Through Slaughter, and Charles Olson on verticality.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Bobbie Louise Hawkins lecture, The sounding word, July, 1989.

docs.creator: Whalen, Philip
docs.description: Final portion of a Philip Whalen lecture. This portion of the lecture is just a series of questions and answers primarily dealing with vocabulary: its importance and ways to improve. Series 87P047 and 87P048
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Whalen lecture part 2 June 1987

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen; Hawkins, Bobbie Louise; Taylor, Steven; Waldman, Anne
docs.description: Second half of a reading with Allen Ginsberg, Bobbie Louise Hawkins, Anne Waldman, and Steven Taylor. This portion of the reading features Waldman and Ginsberg. (Continued from 89P045)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg, Anne Waldman, Steven Taylor and Bobbi Louise Hawkins performance, July, 1989.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen; Lande, Art
docs.description: Allen Ginsberg sings at the West End Tavern in Boulder, Colorado, accompanied by a jazz ensemble with Art Lande. Highlights include "Hum bom," "Put down your cigarette rag (Don't smoke)," and "Sickness blues."
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg and jazz ensemble at the West End Tavern, Boulder, Colorado, July, 1991.

docs.creator: Allen Ginsberg
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg The History of Poetry pt. 12

docs.creator: Rothenberg, Jerome
docs.description: Second half of a Jerome Rothenberg class on ethnopoetics and performance, discussing shamanism, performance as ritual, gaining knowledge through experience, meditation, Seneca songs, being prisoners of language, trance and illusionism. Part 4 of a series. (Continued from 81P022A)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Jerome Rothenberg class on ethnopoetics and performance, August, 1981, part 4.

docs.creator: Carroll, Jim
docs.description: The second half of a Jim Carroll class on poetry and music. Carroll disusses jazz, blues, popular music, poetry and his own band. The first third of the tape includes questions and discussion about Allen Ginsberg. (Continued from 86P003)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Jim Carroll class, Poetics and music, June, 1986.

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne; Schelling, Andrew; Warshall, Peter; Wilson, Peter Lamborn
docs.description: First half of a panel on Dharma and eco-poetics, chaired by Andrew Schelling at Naropa's Summer Writing program, with Joanne Kyger, Peter Lamborn Wilson, and Peter Warshall. Schelling asks the panel to look at strategies for writers interested in environmental issues. Wilson and Warshall talk about the politics of environmentalism. Kyger points out that ecology begins at home with a "Zen awareness" of the household. The panel ends with a question and answer session. (Continued on 96P009)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Andrew Schelling, Peter Lamborn Wilson, Peter Warshall, and Joanne Kyger panel, Dharma and eco-poetics, June, 1996.

docs.creator: Snyder, Gary
docs.description: Gary Snyder chairs a colloquium consisting of unnamed faculty members in which they discuss art in terms of right occupation, entertainment. product, process, morality, quality, and one's audience.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Snyder Colloquium August 1983

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: This first class of Waldman's graduate Gertrude Stein seminar centers on Stein's book The Autobiography of Alice B. Toklas. The class discusses their reading of the text in-depth and Waldman lectures on Stein's earlier life, her teachers, brother and her relationship with Alice B. Toklas.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman Class September 1989

docs.creator: Collom, Jack; Creeley, Robert; Rakosi, Carl
docs.description: Jack Collom, Robert Creeley, and Carl Rakosi reading. Collom reads "Pawnee Pass," "Wild goose," "Dead birds," "Le specter de la rose," and others. Creeley reads "Flaubert's early prose," "The place," "Arroyo," "If I had my way," and others. Rakosi reads "The weightlifter," "The voice of the people," "The old codger's lament," "Ground breaking," "Ten meditations," and others.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Jack Collom, Carl Rakosi, Robert Creeley reading, June, 1998.

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne
docs.description: A classroom lecture, "Beat And Other Rebel Angels," delivered by Joanne Kyger October 22, 1991. Continuing her lecture series Kyger gives an "oral biography" of the poet Gary Snyder.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Joanne Kyger beat rebel angels class 3 October 1991

docs.creator: Retallack, Joan; Thomas, Lorenzo
docs.description: Second half of a reading, with Joan Retallack and Lorenzo Thomas. Retallack reads a long poem entitled, "Lost briefcase conjecture," and Thomas reads "Whale song," "Equinox," and others. (Continued from 02P084)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Joan Retallack and Lorenzo Thomas reading, July, 2002.

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne
docs.description: This is class 11 in Joanne Kyger's summer of 1981 series Compassion for Place. In this class Kyger lectures on "Maya Land," the remaining peoples of the Chiapas Mexico-Guatemala borders, with particular emphasis on the Tzotzil speakers. She reads stories from their mythology, and some of her own works from her visit to the area, and discusses the fusion of their iconography with that of Christianity. Then the final 30 minutes of the class mostly consists of students reading their own work. This is class 11 of 12
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Joanne Kyger class 11 June 1981

docs.creator: Burke, Junior
docs.description: Junior Burke performs "On The Street Where You Live" on guitar. The song becomes the platform for a funny coming of age tale of his early life in Illinois.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Junior Burke performs February 1983

docs.creator: Wilson, Peter Lamborn
docs.description: First half of a lecture by Peter Lamborn Wilson. Wilson plays a few music CDs followed followed by a discussion of William S. Burroughs's book The Western Lands, Marco Polo, Caliph of Cairo, Mongol raids, Arthur Rimbaud and other topics. (Continues on 99P052)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.subject: none
docs.title: Peter Lamborn Wilson lecture, June, 1999.

docs.creator: Ping, Wang; Sze, Arthur
docs.description: Second half of a reading, with Wang Ping and Arthur Sze. Ping reads "Of flesh and spirit," "Song of calling souls" and "Ultimate passage." Sze reads poems from his book Archipelago, including "Original memory" and "Archipelago." (Continued from 95P027)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Wang Ping and Arthur Sze reading, June, 1995.

docs.creator: Collom, Jack; Hawkins, Bobbie Louise; Waldman, Anne
docs.description: A memorial reading for Robert Duncan recorded Oct. 18, 1988 at Naropa featuring Anne Waldman, Bobbie Louise Hawkins, Jack Collom and others.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Robert Duncan Memorial October 1988

docs.creator: Sanchez, Sonia
docs.description: Sonia Sanchez reads "Middle Passage," "Wounded in the House of a Friend," and others. Talks about peace activism and changing perceptions of it post-9/11, and about her work. This is part 2 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Faculty reading with Baraka, Prevallet, Richards part 2 June 2004

docs.creator: Warshall, Peter
docs.description: A Peter Warshall lecture discussing animals sounds and the nature of music and speech. Warshall plays various animal sounds, talks about how sounds are created and the abilities of the human ear to hear sounds. He discusses a variety of related topics, including the evolution of vowels and consonants, sacred sounds and semantics.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Peter Warshall lecture, Two billion years of animal sounds, June, 1999.

docs.creator: Bye, Reed
docs.description: Reed Bye, Hamlet, August 1980. Reed Bye presents a class in the series "Rotating Shakespeare" on the play Hamlet. Bye describes the history of criticism on Hamlet and the origins of the Hamlet story, then presents a cosmological interpretation of Hamlet. The class then reads through the play, interspersing the reading with discussion of individual scenes. (Continued on 80P162). This is class 1 of 4.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Reed Bye class 1 August 1980

docs.creator: Bye, Reed
docs.description: Reed Bye, Hamlet, August 1980. Reed Bye presents a class on Shakespeare's Hamlet. In this class, Bye and the students continue their reading of Hamlet, debating the timing of the seduction of Gertrude and focusing on the appearance of the ghost of the king. (Continued from 80P161). This is class 2 of 4
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Reed Bye class 2 August 1980

docs.creator: Grenier, Robert
docs.description: The first tape in a series of tapes that cover a class given by Robert Grenier that covers topics of language, place, and the object. He gives reference to many artists including Larry Eigner and reads some of Eigner's work.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Robert Grenier on language part 1 July 1992

docs.creator: Blaser, Robin
docs.description: A lecture by Robin Blaser involving the reading of pieces by various artists including Blaser as well as discussion. Topics of readings and discussion includes the topic of "irreparables" the philosophies and terms surrounding it.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Robin Blaser Lecture subject of irreparables July 1995

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: A snippet of material that may conclude a class on the history of poetry by Allen Ginsberg, from a class series during the summer of 1975. The recording includes three minutes and six seconds of Ginsberg talking about the morality of William Carlos Williams and the subject of poetry and peception. (Possibly continued from 75P021)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class, The history of poetry, part 20, June, 1975.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen; Taylor, Steven; Waldman, Anne
docs.description: First half of a performance of music and poetry with Steven Taylor, Anne Waldman, and Allen Ginsberg. Taylor sings "Who pays the piper calls the tune," "King cotton," and others. Waldman's performance includes "Artemis," "Mother's curse," and "Cut." (Continued on 88P018)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg, Anne Waldman and Steven Taylor performance, July, 1988.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: First half of a class about the history of poetry by Allen Ginsberg, from a series of classes during the summer of 1975. Ginsberg discusses the American poet, and one of his mentors, William Carlos Williams. Ginsberg reads selections from Williams's work, and discusses his style and background. (Continues on 75P021)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class, The history of poetry, part 18, June, 1975.

docs.creator: Corso, Gregory; Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: A class on the history of poetry by Allen Ginsberg, in a series of classes in the Summer of 1975. Gregory Corso helps teach the class. Percy Bysshe Shelley and Thomas Hood are discussed extensively. The class reads from Shelley, and Ginsberg recites Shelley's "Ode to the west wind."
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class, The history of poetry, part 3, June, 1975

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Allen Ginsberg class on Beat literary history of the 1950's, discussing William S. Burroughs's book Junky and his first meeting with Herman Hunke. Ginsbergs discusses passages from the book, including teaheads (page 17), informers (page 47), fags (page 72), the Rio Grande Valley (page 105) and interzone prototypes (page 111). Part 2 of a 20 part series.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg class, Literary history of the Beat generation, the 50's, part 2, March, 1981.

docs.creator: Eshleman, Clayton
docs.description: The third class in a series of three taught by Clayton Eshleman. Topics of discussion include Cesar Vallejo and Vallejo's work, the translation of his work, and the topic of translation at large.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Clayton Eschleman class part 2

docs.creator: Warshall, Peter
docs.description: A lecture with Peter Warshall discussing the battle to preserve Mt. Graham, its endangered Red Squirrel, and the relevant bio-politics that emerge from the issue. Keywords: ecology and literature, biopolitics
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Peter Warshall lecture on squirrels on earth and stars above.

docs.creator: Katz, Eliot; Levitsky, Rachel
docs.description: A reading, June 19, 2004 held at Naropa University including Eliot Katz and Rachel Levitsky. Katz reads new and old poem. Levitsky reads a selection of her translations of Zhang Er and ends with a lengthy reading from her manuscript in progress Neighbor. This is part 1 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Reading with Katz, Levitsky part 1 June 2004

docs.creator: Cage, John
docs.description: First half of an interview and performance by John Cage. He discusses his "Empty words" concert, Henry David Thoreau, modern art, and "Mureau," a work combining music and Thoreau. (Continues on A002B)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: John Cage interview and performance, Empty words, August, 1974.

docs.creator: Creeley, Robert
docs.description: First half of a Robert Creeley lecture on the origins, history, politics, and techniques of language poetry. He looks at how language poetry evolved out of earlier styles as well as its influence on contemporary poets. Topics include the ideas of Charles Bernstein, the work of Charles Olson, William Carlos Williams, Robert Duncan, Ezra Pound, and many others, as well as the possibilities for using words without referents. (Continued on 84P010)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Robert Creeley lecture on language poetry, July, 1984.

docs.creator: Whalen, Philip
docs.description: Second half of Class 8 of "In the Pressure Tank" series held at Naropa Institute between July 23 and August 20, 1980. (The whole series is contained on 80P093-115.) Philip Whalen discusses Wallace Stevens's poem "Academic Discourse at Havana." Specific attention is given to French poets--Stephane Mallarme, Paul Valery, Andre Gide, and others--who influenced Stevens. (Continued from 80p105.) Keywords: New American Poetry, West Coast poetry, Buddhism, American modernist poetry, symbolism
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: In the pressure tank, Class 8

docs.creator: Gilbert, Alan
docs.description: First half of a Naropa Summer Writing Program Faculty Reading, with Alan Gilbert reading five poems, including an excerpt from "The subjects of kings, of falcon alert." (Continues on 00P084)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Alan Gilbert reading, July, 2000.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: The first class in an Allen Ginsberg course on Expansive Poetics. Ginsberg opens the class with a brief history of the topics of courses he has taught in the past. He then explains his expectations for this course and the material he plans to cover in the sourcebook/anthology he is compiling. He then reads Geza Roheim's Children of the desert, Shelley's Hymn to intellectual beauty, Ode to the West Wind and the end of Adonais. The class discusses rhythm and the expansive breath and how it influences one's work.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Class part 1

docs.creator: Wilson, Peter Lamborn
docs.description: Second half of a Peter Lamborn Wilson lecture about the art of Sufi traveling. He continues his discussion on nomads followed by a brief talk about the travels of French poet Arthur Rimbaud. He ends the lecture discussing the future of travel. (Continued from 91P149)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Peter Lamborn Wilson lecture, Sacred drift: the art of Sufi travel, July, 1991.

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne
docs.description: A workshop, "Beat And Other Rebel Angels," taught by Joanne Kyger at the Naropa Institute October 1991. Kyger speaks extensively about the poet Jack Spicer; his work, his life and his death. Along the way Kyger comments on various central and ancillary figures populating the San Francisco Northbeach scence at mid-century.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Joanne Kyger beat rebel angels class 1 October 1991

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne
docs.description: A class, "Beat And Other Rebel Angel's," taught by Joanne Kyger October 30, 1991. Tape 2 of 2, Kyger begins with a class read through of Whalen's poem "To The Muse," and ends with a brief discussion of Philip Whalen's novels.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Joanne Kyger beat rebel angels class 5 October 1991

docs.creator: Dorn, Ed
docs.description: The final part of a class by Ed Dorn on writing and Black Mountain. In this part of the class, Dorn briefly discusses the similarities between Black Mountain College and The Naropa Institute as well as Robert Creeley and Charles Olson's involvement in Black Mountain College. Tape 2 of 2.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Ed Dorn class part 3 June 1977

docs.creator: Waldman, Anne
docs.description: First half of an Anne Waldman class on women writers from the summer of 1977. Waldman focuses on the poets Sei Shonagon, Collette, Helen Adam, Denise Levertov, Sylvia Plath, Joanne Kyger, and Bernadette Mayer. Waldman plays several audio cassettes of the poets reading their own work. (Continues on 77P080)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anne Waldman class, Women writers, August, 1977.

docs.creator: Hollo, Anselm
docs.description: A class taught by Anselm Hollo July 31, 1980 at the Naropa Institute. The series concludes with Hollo and class informally discussing politics and translation. This is part 3 of 3.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anselm Hollo class part 3 July 1980

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne; Schelling, Andrew; Warshall, Peter; Wilson, Peter Lamborn
docs.description: Second half of a panel on Dharma and eco-poetics, chaired by Andrew Schelling at Naropa's Summer Writing program, with Joanne Kyger, Peter Lamborn Wilson, and Peter Warshall. Schelling asks the panel to look at strategies for writers interested in environmental issues. Wilson and Warshall talk about the politics of environmentalism. Kyger points out that ecology begins at home with a "Zen awareness" of the household. The panel ends with a question and answer session. (Continued on 96P009)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Andrew Schelling, Peter Lamborn Wilson, Peter Warshall, and Joanne Kyger panel, Dharma and eco-poetics, June, 1996.

docs.creator: Collom, Jack; Corbett, William; Hollo, Anselm; Kyger, Joanne; Mackey, Nathaniel

docs.creator: Prevallet, Kristin
docs.description: A Kristin Prevallet lecture, "A Poem is never by itself alone," July 2001. Prevallet talks about investigative poetics: inquiry and investigative aspects. She reads from an essay about the philosophical principles of (relational) investigative poetics mentioning Olson's "total concentration," Manuel De Landa's book "A Thousand Years of Nonlinear History," and the inspiration question of an investigative poet, then gives practical examples. There is a question and answer session in which Prevallet talks about issues of representation in the field of investigative poetics.

docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Anselm Hollo lecture, Greek anthology, June, 1986.

docs.creator: Bye, Reed; Waldman, Anne; Whalen, Philip
docs.description: Reed Bye, Hamlet, August 1980. Philip Whalen, Pericles, August 1980. On the first half of the recording, Reed Bye continues his class on Shakespeare's "Hamlet," focusing on Hamlet's conversations with Ophelia and Gertrude. In the second half, Philip Whalen presents a class on Shakespeare's "Pericles," concentrating on anachronisms in the play, its staging, and the educational background of the playwrights and audiences of Shakespeare's period. docs.creator: Carroll, Jim
docs.description: First half of the second installment of Jim Carroll's class on poetry and music. Carroll plays recordings of his songs as well as songs from Phil Ochs. He also discusses his collaboration with Doors musician Ray Manzerick, conversations with Lou Reed, and how he approaches the difference between writing lyrics, music, and poetry. (Continues on 86P006)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Jim Carroll class, Poetics and music, June, 1986.

docs.creator: Bye, Reed
docs.description: Reed Bye, Hamlet, August 1980. Reed Bye presents a class in the series "Rotating Shakespeare" on the play Hamlet. Bye describes the history of criticism on Hamlet and the origins of the Hamlet story, then presents a cosmological interpretation of Hamlet. The class then reads through the play, interspersing the reading with discussion of individual scenes. (Continued on 80P162). This is class 1 of 4.

The class also continues the discussion of the goddess in female writing and is introduced to the work and artistry of Jane Austen. (Continues on 77p071.)

docs.description: Second half of a panel on jazz featuring Clark Coolidge, Steve Lacy, Nathaniel Mackey and Robert Creeley. Coolidge, who worked as a jazz drummer at one time, begins by reading his piece "A note on bop." The panelists move on to a discussion of bop as a language, jazz as sound poetry, rhythm, the relationship of words and dance to music, and their own experiences with jazz. They also touch briefly on the work of Harry Partch. (Continued from 91P067)

docs.creator: Blaser, Robin; Hawkins, Bobbie Louise
docs.description: A Robin Blaser lecture titled Belief, doubt and politics. Blaser discusses Clayton Eshelman, Ralph Waldo Emerson's "Lecture on the times," surrealism and romanticism, Victor Hugo, crucifixes and virgins, Francis Fukuyama and the end of history, Hanna Arendt, Lucian's "Zeus Rants," Robin Blaser's "Rose, Jack and Rexella Van Imp, Sappho and Ann Carsons, Martha Nussbaum, Ariadne and the soul as spider. The lecture ends with a question and answer session. (Part 1 of a two part lecture series.)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Robin Blaser lecture, Belief, doubt and politics, Part 1, July, 1992.

docs.creator: Wilson, Peter Lamborn
docs.description: Second half of part 1, of a two-part class, by Peter Lamborn Wilson on utopian poetics. Wilson discusses "imaginal quanta," education, the role of the poet in utopia, the unity of the fulfillment of individual and group, the role of apocalypse in Western thought, and the role of abstract thought in the human transformation from foraging to agriculture.(Continued from 93P066)
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Peter Lamborn Wilson class, Utopian poetics, part 1, July, 1993.

docs.creator: Gilbert, Alan
docs.description: A lecture on documentary poetry and cultural poetics by Alan Gilbert. The lecture includes music and ends with a question and answer period. [by Ann] Alan Gilbert lectures on art, literature, and culture. He discusses works of art as social documentary, alleging that all art is site specific, all cultures are hybrid, and works of art have different effects in different contexts. He uses Walker Evans's photographs, Harry Smith's recordings of folk music, Anselm Hollo's poem High plains drifting and many other examples to illustrate his ideas.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Alan Gilbert lecture on documentary poetics, July, 2000.

docs.creator: Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Allen Ginsberg class on Expansive Poetics. He opens by talking about Pushkin and reads his "The Prophet," "Message to Syberia" and a couple others. He then moves to American `19th century authors and talks about Edgar Allen Poe and reads "The Bells" and "Anabelle Lee." He then talks about rhythm and the spondee and goes into great details explaining and giving examples of different meters. He defines meter and foot. Then he moves into Herman Mellville and reads "Billy in the Darbies," "The housetop a night piece" and "to ned bund." He then closes the class by reading and discussing sections of Walt Whitman's "Song of myself." This is part of a long series
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg Class part 2 June 1981

docs.creator: Charters, Ann; Ginsberg, Allen
docs.description: Allen Ginsberg and Ann Charters class on Jack Kerouac and Russian Futurists, discussing Kerouac's method of revision, his five-cent notebooks, his book Old Angel Midnight, methods of composition, his 1956-1959 notebooks, James Joyce's Molly Bloom and Finnegan's Wake, Buddhist Shakespearean plays, Kerouac's On the Road scroll, Visions of Cody and Dharma Bums, and a short discussion of the Russian Futurists.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Allen Ginsberg and Ann Charters class on Jack Kerouac and Russian Futurists, July, 1981.

creator: Myles, Eileen
Oliver, Akilah
docs.description: An Eileen Myles lecture, "Friendship: the force of community in poetry and prose." Myles discusses the role of friendship and poetry in bringing one's inner world, which she likens to the world of her early friendships with women, to the outer world, which she relates to her early friendships with men. She discusses the growing laterality of the art world and emphasizes the defining importance of context.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Eileen Myles lecture, Friendship: the force of community in poetry and prose, June, 2000.

docs.creator: Snyder, Gary
docs.description: Gary Snyder leads a class called "Linguistics, Anthropology." Snyder's discussions of indigenous, oral poetic traditions, and his reading of "The Song of the Daughter of the Mountain God," a poem from the oral tradition of the peoples indigenous to Hokaido, Japan, lead him to discuss the basic linguistics of speech.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Gary Snyder Linguistics class part 1 1983

docs.creator: Kyger, Joanne
docs.description: This is class III of Compassion for Place, a series taught by Joanne Kyger at the Naropa Institute in 1981. Kyger continues to discuss Coyote and read Coyote stories, but widens the discussion to its image as the trickster, and how Coyote can also be female. She reads from Snyder's The Old Ways, and talks about his Coyote Journal. A large part of the recording focuses on students in the class reading their nature-based assignments, created by visiting the same individual outdoor space alone over a period of weeks. This is class 3 of 12.
docs.publisher: Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics
docs.title: Joanne Kyger class 3 June 1981

docs.description: The first two classes in a "History of poetry" series by Allen Ginsberg in the summer of 1975, taught by Gregory Corso while Ginsberg was sick. Corso holds the class in a "Socratic" format, allowing the students to ask him questions about anything they wish. He describes his process of editing and shaping a poem, and also talks about his family and relations with members of the Beat generation.

docs.description: Harry Smith describes two Native American ceremonies he witnessed in the early 1940's in the Pacific Northwest. docs.creator: Burroughs, William S.
docs.description: Second half of a workshop with William S. Burroughs comparing his works to those of Jack Kerouac, discussing their writing techniques. Burroughs provides biographical information on where the two met and their relationship. He also discusses what it means to be a writer and how many people are not writers even though they claim to be and have published work. Burroughs responds to questions about his relationship with Kerouac, dreams, and his own literary influences. This workshop took place during the 1982 Jack Kerouac Conference at the Naropa Institute.(Continued from 82p267A.) Keywords: beat movement, history of beat movement, 20th century literature
